Most of my students believe that fluent speakers never hesitate. So I ask them to listen to ten minutes of any podcast and count. They are always shocked. Native speakers hesitate all the time. The difference is what they do while they hesitate. They do not go silent. They say, let me think about that, or, I mean, or, what I am trying to say is. Those phrases carry no information at all, and that is exactly their job. They tell the other person that you are still in the conversation and that the sentence is coming. Silence does the opposite. After about three seconds, the listener starts to wonder whether you have understood the question. So the goal is not to stop hesitating. The goal is to hesitate out loud.
